questions.question: What will help a person recover from drinking alcohol?
questions.explanation: Only time will help a person recover from the effects of alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. This sign tells you that a sharp turn is coming. Reduce your speed.

questions.question: When are seat belts most effective?

options.text: When passengers wear them on long drives.
When all passengers wear them on expressways.
When everyone in the car wears one every time.

questions.correctAnswerText: When everyone in the car wears one every time.
questions.explanation: Everyone in a vehicle should wear a seat belt every trip. Without a seat belt, a person can become a flying object in a crash and hurt others.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm out?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk and pass on the left side.
Keep driving when kids are done exiting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: You must stop completely when you see a school bus with its stop arm out. Do not move until the arm is raised.

questions.question: What should you do when you see a steady green light?

options.text: Go through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
Stop if a police officer is nearby.
Treat it like a four-way stop.
Come to a complete stop first.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go through, unless vehicles or pedestrians are in the intersection.
questions.explanation: At a steady green light, let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first. You can proceed, but be ready to slow down or stop if the light changes.

questions.question: A driver ahead is driving with one hand and talking to a passenger. What should you do?

options.text: Know that this driver is not paying full attention.
Do not drive the same way.

questions.explanation: Stay away from distracted drivers. Give them extra space because they are more likely to crash. Never drive the same way.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that an intersection is coming. Watch for traffic crossing your path.

questions.question: What type of sign is diamond-shaped?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped and yellow. They warn about hazards or areas with special rules ahead.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the divided highway is ending.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot park here. Regulation signs tell you what you must or must not do.

questions.question: You must stop your vehicle at:

options.text: A stop sign at an intersection.
When a traffic officer tells you to stop.

questions.explanation: You must stop your vehicle at stop signs, red lights, and whenever a traffic officer orders you to stop.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is tailgating you, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
Make eye contact with the driver.
Speed up while the driver is passing you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you encounter an aggressive driver, move out of their way. Do not make eye contact or try to challenge them by speeding up, as this will only make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When is it okay to text while driving?

options.text: If you can text without looking at your phone.
If you only look away from the road for a moment.

questions.explanation: Texting while driving is illegal. Using a cell phone while driving is a serious distraction that can cause accidents.

questions.question: What is the correct way to change lanes?

options.text: Check your mirrors and signal, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
Signal, check your mirrors, then change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Signal, check your mirrors, look over your shoulder for blind spots, then change lanes.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, signal in the direction you want to go. Check your rearview and side mirrors. Look over your shoulder to check for blind spots. Only change lanes when it is safe.

questions.question: When driving in fog, you should use your:
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog. High beams bounce off the fog and reduce your visibility. Fog lights can also help if your vehicle has them.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle?
questions.explanation: All occupants of a vehicle must wear seat belts whenever the vehicle is moving. This applies to drivers, front seat passengers, and back seat passengers. Seat belts are required even if the vehicle has airbags.

questions.question: If you take an over-the-counter medication, you should:

options.text: Drive regardless of any warnings on the label.

questions.explanation: Many over-the-counter medications can affect your driving ability. Check the label for warnings before you drive. If you are unsure, ask your doctor or pharmacist whether it is safe to drive while taking the medication.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns that a divided highway is ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads with a divider in the middle. You must keep to the right.

questions.question: If a tire blows out while you are driving, what should you do?

options.text: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
Keep your current speed and steer straight.
Swerve back and forth to alert other drivers.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep the steering wheel straight and slowly release the gas pedal.
questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly and keep the car straight. Remove your foot from the gas pedal slowly. Do not brake hard. Once you have control, brake gently and pull off the road to a safe location.

questions.question: Driving ability can be impaired by:
questions.explanation: Safe driving requires you to be in good physical condition. Your driving can be impaired by alcohol, medications, and drowsiness.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs warn you that the road curves sharply in the direction the chevron points. In this case, it curves left. You may see several chevron signs throughout the curve.

questions.question: How can alcohol affect you while driving?
questions.explanation: Alcohol affects your brain's control of judgment and self-control. It slows your reaction time and coordination. It also impairs your vision and your ability to judge distance.

questions.question: When passing an emergency vehicle on the side of the road, you should:

options.text: Move to another lane or slow down.
Ask the emergency worker if they need help.
Move to the lane closest to the emergency vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to another lane or slow down.
questions.explanation: When you pass an emergency vehicle on the roadside, you must move away from its lane. If you cannot move safely to another lane, you must slow down.

questions.question: You approach a railroad crossing with no train in sight or sound. You must stop if:
questions.explanation: Stop before crossing railroad tracks if flashing red lights are on, a gate is lowered, a stop sign is posted, a flagger signals you to stop, or a train is visible or too close for safe crossing. Never race a train.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Always stop, whether a stop sign is posted or not.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.
Be ready to help children cross the street.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Always give pedestrians the right of way when they are in or about to enter a crosswalk. Stay alert for pedestrians at intersections and when turning.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road to the right is one-way traffic only.
There is a detour to the right due to roadwork.
Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
There is a crossroad to your right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down because the road ahead turns sharply.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road ahead turns sharply in the direction shown. You should slow down as if you were making a turn at an intersection.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign warns of a hill ahead.

questions.question: You miss your exit on the freeway. What should you do?

options.text: Make a U-turn through the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer for help.

questions.explanation: Take the next exit if you miss yours. Never stop, back up, or cross the median on a highway. Do not swerve across lanes at the last second. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: You hear a siren behind you. What should you do?

options.text: Pull over to the right and stop.
Speed up to get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over to the right and stop.
questions.explanation: When you hear a siren or see flashing lights behind you, slow down and safely pull over to the right side of the road. In heavy traffic, keep moving slowly until you can get out of the emergency vehicle's way.

questions.question: It starts to rain while you are driving. What should you do?

options.text: Drive at the maximum speed limit.
Drive close behind the vehicle in front of you.

questions.explanation: When heavy rain reduces visibility, reduce your speed. Turn on your headlights so others can see you. If rain is so heavy you cannot see clearly, pull onto the shoulder and stop until it stops.
